newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania differs with U.S. stance on NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Romania differs with U.S. stance on NATO expansion.

text.p: Romania's Foreign Minister said on Thursday the U.S. decision to favour rapid NATO membership for only three ex-communist states -- Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- did not serve Washington's interests in eastern Europe.

"We don't share this point of view," Adrian Severin told a news conference. "This decision does not protect sufficiently U.S. interests in this region." The U.S. position, announced at a NATO meeting in Brussels, left longshot hopefuls Romania and Slovenia off the list of proposed first entrants.
Romania differs with U.S. stance on NATO expansion
Severin suggested that the United States could be persuaded to change its mind ahead of the NATO summit in Madrid next month where the new candidates for membership are to be announced.

"The final formula of NATO's first-wave expansion will only be known at Madrid," he said. "By then, we are sure that the U.S. administration will take into consideration all the pertinent arguments in our favour."

Bucharest's centrist leaders have led a high-profile campaign to persuade the United States and Germany to end their reservations over Romania's bid. France and other members from NATO's southern flank have backed the Balkan country.

Centrist President Emil Constantinescu, who ousted an ex-communist in elections last year, will meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Bonn on July 2 in a last-ditch attempt to rally German support. Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea travels to Washington next week to lobby support in the U.S. Senate.
